title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. This includes refusing to rent, terminating, or charging a higher deposit or rent based on criminal history. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond.
key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use banned; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
coverage_conditions: Current and prospective tenants of rental housing in Berkeley, including advertising, application, leasing, tenancy, and family-member additions.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions for lifetime sex offender applicants, public housing/Section 8 properties (limited), owner move-back rental agreements under BMC 13.76.130 A.9, and existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates; owner-occupied 1-3 unit exemption requires owner residence as primary residence.

quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
conflict_note: The page gives only the City Council passage date (April 14, 2020), not the effective date. The ordinance is treated as in force because the Rent Board is administering complaints under it.

title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance payment (2026 inflation-adjusted amounts)
requirement: Owners who evict a tenant for owner move-in must pay relocation assistance. For 2026 the standard payment is $19,413, with an additional $6,471 for qualifying households, indexed annually to Bay Area CPI.
key_value: $19,413 standard; additional $6,471 for qualifying households (effective 2026-01-01; 1.5% CPI adjustment)
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance who are evicted for owner move-in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when an owner move-in eviction occurs; additional payment depends on the household meeting qualifying criteria not stated in the document.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (relocation assistance provisions)
quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.
conflict_note: Effective date and enacted date refer to the 2026 inflationary adjustment approved by the Rent Board on 2025-10-16, not the original ordinance enactment. Document does not give the municipal code section number or define qualifying households.

title: Ellis Act withdrawal eviction relocation assistance payment (2026 inflation-adjusted amounts)
requirement: Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions. For 2026 this is $19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households.
key_value: $19,413 standard; additional $6,471 for qualifying households (effective 2026-01-01)
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley evicted because the owner is withdrawing the property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when an Ellis Act withdrawal eviction occurs; additional payment depends on the household meeting qualifying criteria not stated in the document.

quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.
conflict_note: Dates refer to the 2026 inflationary adjustment approved 2025-10-16, not the ordinance's original enactment. Document does not give the municipal code section number.

title: California tenant screening fee cap and itemization requirements
requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to the annually adjusted state maximum and only for actual screening costs. They must give the applicant a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket costs and time spent, a copy of any credit report obtained, and a refund of any unused portion.
key_value: $68.96 maximum for 2026 (annually adjusted)
coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents charging prospective residential tenants a fee to screen applications in California.
quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
conflict_note: The $68.96 figure is the 2026 inflation-adjusted cap as reported by the Berkeley Rent Board. The page attributes the duty to accept a reusable screening report to § 1950.6; that duty may arise under a separate provision (§ 1950.1).

title: No screening fee when no unit is available; refund to unselected applicants
requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must return fees to applicants not selected, unless it reviews applications first-come-first-served and does not charge applicants who are not considered.
coverage_conditions: Landlords charging screening fees to prospective residential tenants in California.
exemptions: Landlords using a first-come-first-served policy who do not charge applicants who are not considered need not refund.
quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
conflict_note: The page states this as current law but does not tie it to a specific subsection or effective date.

title: Required tenant screening fee rights statement
requirement: An owner who charges an application or credit-report fee must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement before receiving the fee. The owner must also state the maximum fee permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b), either in the application or in a separate disclosure.
coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of residential property in Berkeley who charge applicants a screening or application fee.
quoted_span: The “Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement” shall mean the following statement or a substantially similar statement:
conflict_note: The statement's required URL is still to be provided by the City, so the exact disclosure text is not finalized.

title: Ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate's departure or to adding or replacing a roommate. Under BMC 13.78.018, the rule applies regardless of contrary lease terms.
coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, including existing leases.
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
requirement: Landlords of fully covered units may raise rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board using a CPI-based formula. Measure BB caps the AGA at 5%, though banked unused AGAs from prior years may still be applied to reach the rent ceiling.
key_value: AGA tied to CPI, max 5%
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units, chiefly most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, and single-family homes with five or more individually rented rooms. Fully covered government-owned or subsidized units now also have a rent ceiling.
exemptions: Partially covered units (new construction with a certificate of occupancy issued after 1980, most single-family homes, most condominiums) have no rent ceiling. Shared kitchen/bath units are exempt only if the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy. Banked AGAs may exceed 5% to reach the rent ceiling.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family homes are fully covered only if the tenancy began before 1996 or five or more rooms are rented individually. Shared kitchen/bath exemption depends on landlord residence. Subsidized-unit coverage depends on the subsidy type and HUD mortgage status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
conflict_note: Page does not state Measure BB's effective date or a municipal code section. The 1980 cutoff is described both as 'built before 1980' (fully covered) and as 'certificate of occupancy issued after 1980' (new construction, partially covered), so treatment of 1980 itself is ambiguous.

title: Government-owned or subsidized units now covered by Rent Ordinance
requirement: Government-owned or subsidized units (e.g., Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME) must be registered as fully or partially covered and pay an annual registration fee. Fully covered subsidized units have a rent ceiling limited by the AGA.
coverage_conditions: Government-owned or subsidized units. Whether a unit is fully or partially covered depends on unit type and any federal or state preemption.
exemptions: The following are partially covered (no rent ceiling) regardless of unit type: Section 202 and Section 811 units, and Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside, and Project-based Section 8 units in projects with HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgages.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Depends on the subsidy type and whether the project has a HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgage.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Government-owned or -subsidized rental units become either fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated on page.

title: Rent increase petitions only for completed capital improvements
requirement: Landlords may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements. They can no longer obtain preliminary authorization for planned improvements.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units subject to the rent ceiling.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).
conflict_note: Effective date not stated on page.

title: Utility charges must be in base rent unless separately metered
requirement: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024 in fully covered units, landlords may charge for utilities only as part of base rent, or where the utility is separately metered and in the tenant's name under the lease. Adding utility costs to the rent ceiling requires a Rent Board petition.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units; tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024.
exemptions: Separately metered utilities placed in the tenant's name as required by the lease.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy start date on or after 2024-02-06; utility metering arrangement.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Utility charges must be a set amount incorporated into the base rent at the start of a tenancy unless the utility is separately metered and the account is in the tenant’s name as specified in the lease.
conflict_note: The February 6, 2024 applicability date predates the November 2024 election that passed Measure BB; this may be retroactive application or a typo. Categorized under rent limits because it governs charges beyond the rent ceiling.

title: Just cause required for evictions from fully or partially covered units
requirement: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted without just cause (formerly called good cause).
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units, including new construction, most single-family homes and condos, and government-subsidized units.
exemptions: Exempt units, including units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath with a landlord who lived on the property at the start of the tenancy.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Shared kitchen/bath exemption depends on the landlord residing on the property before the tenancy began.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause)
quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
conflict_note: Page does not give a code citation or the original enactment date.

title: No nonpayment eviction for debt under one month's Fair Market Rent
requirement: A landlord may evict for nonpayment only if the tenant owes rental debt at least equal to one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent-size unit in the Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR area for the fiscal year in which rent is demanded.
key_value: >= 1 month HUD FMR (Oakland-Fremont)
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is no longer permitted for rental debt of less than one month’s Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated on page.

title: No eviction for failing to sign a substantially similar lease
requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires. Measure BB eliminated this just cause.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated on page.

title: Stricter requirements for lease-violation evictions
requirement: Lease-breach evictions require a mutually agreed material term, substantial actual damage to the landlord, and proof that the tenant's behavior was unreasonable. The prior notice to cease must specify the lease term and describe the violation and resulting harm.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated on page.

title: Eviction notice content and three-business-day filing with Rent Board
requirement: Termination notices must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and include its counseling phone number and website. Copies of termination notices, notices to quit, and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
key_value: File within 3 business days
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.
conflict_note: Effective date not stated on page.

title: Mandatory annual inflation adjustment of owner move-in relocation payments
requirement: The Rent Board must adjust owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts for inflation each year.
coverage_conditions: Owner move-in evictions from covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments to owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts each year.
conflict_note: Effective date and payment amounts not stated on page.

title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) of rent ceilings
requirement: Eligible landlords may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by no more than 1.0% for 2026, effective no earlier than January 1, 2026, after giving required notice. The AGA equals 65% of the Bay Area CPI increase, a formula approved by voters in 2004.
key_value: 1.0% for 2026 (65% of Bay Area CPI change, July 2024-June 2025 CPI 1.5%)
coverage_conditions: Units under Berkeley rent ceilings whose landlords meet the eligibility conditions in Rent Board Regulation 1148 and give the required notice to tenants.
exemptions: The 2026 AGA does not apply to tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Landlord must meet Regulation 1148 eligibility conditions and give required notice; excludes tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01 with Costa-Hawkins-set rents. Building-age and unit-type coverage of Berkeley rent ceilings not stated in this document.

citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A; Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board Regulation 1148
quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy – criminal history screening limits
requirement: Covered housing providers may not use blanket bans on applicants with arrests or convictions and must assess applicants case by case. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when deciding eligibility or eviction.
key_value: Convictions older than 5 years may not be considered
coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Boston Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy. Also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought, or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others' safety. Does not apply to current criminal behavior. Federal or state criminal history requirements that conflict with the policy preempt it.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to housing receiving DND funding and/or land, or to income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction.
conflict_note: This is an administrative policy that applies through DND funding and BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy agreements, not a general ordinance. It is dated February 2017 and the document gives no exact effective date. Its current status as of 2026-10-01 is not confirmed by the document.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy – credit score and credit history limits
requirement: Covered housing providers may not use credit scores to approve or deny applications. Credit history may be used only in place of rental history when rental history is unavailable, and lack of credit history (as opposed to poor credit) is not grounds for rejection.
key_value: No use of credit score; credit history only in lieu of rental history
coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
exemptions: Federal or state law criminal history requirements that conflict with the policy preempt it.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to housing receiving DND funding and/or land, or to income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing
conflict_note: This is an administrative policy for publicly funded and inclusionary units, not a general ordinance. It is dated February 2017 and its current status is not confirmed by the document.

title: FEHA limits on use of criminal history in tenant screening
requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories. Denials based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy suitability or safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time elapsed.
key_value: No arrest-only, sealed/expunged, or juvenile records; no blanket bans
coverage_conditions: Most housing providers and housing-related service providers in California, including landlords, property managers, and tenant screening companies.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (but may not publish discriminatory statements); certain shared-living, senior, and homeless youth housing exceptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption when renting to one additional person

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
conflict_note: Agency summary page; does not give a statutory section number or effective date.

title: FEHA source-of-income discrimination ban
requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on how a tenant pays rent, including Section 8 vouchers, rent relief, SSI/disability benefits, or wages, and may not advertise 'No Section 8' or refuse to complete subsidy program paperwork.
coverage_conditions: Most housing providers in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (except discriminatory advertising remains prohibited).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption when renting to one additional person

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

title: FEHA ban on discriminatory tenant screening
requirement: Screening prospective tenants, including by third-party tenant screening companies, may not discriminate based on a protected characteristic such as race, national origin, citizenship, immigration status, disability, familial status, source of income, or age.
coverage_conditions: Landlords, property managers, and tenant screening companies in California.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person; shared-living single-sex preference; qualifying senior housing; some homeless youth housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy and senior housing qualification exemptions

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Screening prospective tenants – including when done by a third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic
conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service and emotional support animals
requirement: Tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for service animals or emotional support animals allowed as a disability accommodation.
key_value: $0 pet deposit for assistance animals
coverage_conditions: Housing providers covered by FEHA where a tenant with a disability has a service or emotional support animal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant has a disability-related need for a service or emotional support animal

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Service animals and emotional-support animals are not subject to breed, size, or weight restrictions ordinarily applied to pets, and tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them.
conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

title: Ban on higher security deposits based on protected characteristics
requirement: Housing providers may not charge higher security deposits to households with children or to applicants using Section 8 or other rental assistance.
coverage_conditions: Most housing providers in California covered by FEHA.
exemptions: Qualifying senior housing may exclude based on age.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Senior housing qualification

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Prohibiting housing providers from having conditions or rules that discriminate against households with children, such as charging a higher security deposit to households with children or excluding children from playing in common areas open to other tenants.
conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy in restraint of trade (AB 325)
requirement: A person may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, set, or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade under the Cartwright Act. This applies generally, including to landlords setting rents.
key_value: Prohibition on use or distribution of a common pricing algorithm in a conspiracy to restrain trade
coverage_conditions: Any person, other than the end consumer, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm that uses competitor data. It is not limited to housing, so it covers rental pricing.
exemptions: End consumers are excluded from the definition of 'person'.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm (used by two or more persons and using competitor data) as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade.

citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
conflict_note: The document shows only enactment (approved and chaptered October 6, 2025) with no effective date stated. The effective date of January 1, 2026 is inferred from California's default rule for regular-session statutes. The law is a general antitrust statute rather than housing-specific.

title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm while coercing adoption of recommended prices (AB 325)
requirement: A person may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if they coerce another person to set or adopt a price or commercial term recommended by the algorithm for the same or similar products or services in California. This applies generally, including to rental housing pricing.
key_value: Prohibition on coercing adoption of algorithm-recommended prices or terms
coverage_conditions: Any person, other than the end consumer, using or distributing a common pricing algorithm who coerces another to adopt its recommended price or commercial term (for example, level of service, availability, or output) for the same or similar products or services in California.
exemptions: End consumers are excluded from the definition of 'person'.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion of another person to adopt a price or commercial term recommended by a common pricing algorithm.

citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
conflict_note: The document shows only enactment (approved and chaptered October 6, 2025) with no effective date stated. The effective date of January 1, 2026 is inferred from California's default rule for regular-session statutes. The law is a general antitrust statute rather than housing-specific.

title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code 1947.12)
requirement: Over any 12-month period, owners may not raise gross rent by more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. Increases are limited to two per 12-month period for the same tenant, and initial rent for a new tenancy may be set freely (vacancy decontrol).
key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10% per 12 months; max 2 increments
coverage_conditions: Residential real property (dwellings or units intended for human habitation, including mobilehome park units) in California, excluding housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years and other listed exemptions. Applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (mobilehome tenancies: on or after February 18, 2021).
exemptions: Deed- or agreement-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school/college-owned dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable units (e.g., single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, if tenants received the required written exemption notice; owner-occupied duplexes where the owner lived in one unit at the start of tenancy and neither unit is an ADU/JADU; homeowners of mobilehomes.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for separately alienable units depends on owner not being a REIT/corporation/corporate-member LLC and on tenants having received the statutory written exemption notice; owner-occupied duplex exemption depends on owner occupancy; affordable-housing deed restrictions or subsidy agreements; dormitory status.

quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
conflict_note: Current text was repealed and re-added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 290 (SB 567), effective January 1, 2024 and operative April 1, 2024; the underlying cap applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (mobilehome tenancies on or after February 18, 2021). Section sunsets and is repealed as of January 1, 2030.

title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent
requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however labeled, of more than one month's rent on top of first month's rent. Small natural-person landlords may charge up to two months (see separate rule), and an advance payment of six or more months' rent is allowed on leases of six months or longer.
key_value: 1 month's rent
coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling; applies to security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024.
exemptions: Small landlords meeting Civ. Code 1950.5(c)(5) (natural person or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total) may charge up to two months, except to service members; advance payment of at least six months' rent on a lease of six months or longer; agreed fees for tenant-requested alterations.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether the landlord qualifies as a small natural-person landlord under (c)(5), which depends on the owner's whole rental portfolio; whether the tenant is a service member; when the security was collected (before July 1, 2024 is exempt).

quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
conflict_note: The effective date is inferred from (c)(6), which exempts security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

title: Small landlord exception: deposit up to two months' rent
requirement: A landlord that is a natural person (or an LLC whose members are all natural persons) and that owns no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may collect security of up to two months' rent. This exception does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member, and such a landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of the lower cap.
key_value: 2 months' rent
coverage_conditions: Landlord is a natural person (including family trust settlors and beneficiaries) or an LLC with all natural-person members, and owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four rental units in total.
exemptions: Not available when the prospective tenant is a service member; in that case the one-month cap applies.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner must be a natural person, family trust, or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total across the portfolio; tenant must not be a service member.

conflict_note: The four-unit limit applies to the landlord's whole portfolio, not just the building, so max_units 4 is a necessary but not sufficient condition.

title: Service member higher security: written explanation and return within six months
requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher-than-standard security based on credit history, credit score, housing history or a similar factor, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and the reason by lease signing. The extra amount must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
key_value: Extra security returned within 6 months
